invariants.text: The ASH state is a full 9-bit vector in F2^9. All 9 coordinates participate in the algebraic structure.
Normalization is deterministic — the same candidate state always produces the same result.
Normalization fails with a diagnostic for transformation-incompatible states — it does not silently produce a result.
Codeword transformations are XOR-by-codeword: `x' = x ⊕ c` for `c ∈ C ⊂ F2^9`.
Codeword transformations are deterministic and pure — same inputs always produce same outputs with no side effects.
Applying the same codeword twice returns to the original state: `(x ⊕ c) ⊕ c = x`.
The codeword set used by the implementation matches the canonical 16-member set — no invented codewords.
Admissibility classification is deterministic — the same state always maps to the same status.
Every 9-bit vector maps to exactly one admissibility status (given a specified codeword set).
Realm encoding is deterministic — equal valid states produce equal realm encodings.
Realm encoding operates only on valid states — invalid states must be rejected with a diagnostic.
Equal input state + equal transition always produce equal output state.
Transitions operate on full 9-bit states via XOR-by-codeword.
Topology generation is deterministic with stable ordering and lineage.
Every axiom evaluation produces a diagnostic record — no bare pass/fail.
Recovery is deterministic — the same classification always produces the same recovery category.
Fallback selection uses only the canonical fallback-policy registry.
Escalation is monotonic — severity never decreases without external intervention.
No silent healing — every recovery action produces a diagnostic record.
SAFE_HALT is terminal — no transitions from SAFE_HALT.
Planning produces no side effects.
The plan is self-contained — the emitter needs only the plan.
GenerationPlanner does not emit artifacts.
ArtifactEmitter does not invent semantics not present in the plan.
Every diagnostic record conforms to the shared `DiagnosticEnvelope` schema.
Every rule_id conforms to the canonical taxonomy pattern.
The diagnostic chain is complete — every step produces a diagnostic with valid chain references.
No silent omission — diagnostics are never deferred, batched, or suppressed.
